item.content:encoded:
In fact, not it would not help. You see, the alarm clock is not just producing sound, but waves. That means that anything it touches would act as a medium for the waves. This introduces two problems that using a vacuum would produce:

1. Unless you levitated the alarm, the clock would send waves through the container and breaking (or even vaporizing if left on long enough) said container. Even if the container did not break, it would cause severe seismic activity.

2. At our current level of knowledge, the human race has not found a way to suck out all of the material within a container. The closest we have ever gotten to a perfect vacuum is 100 mere atoms. Which is by no means a small feat, but not enough. The atoms would eventually be launched at such high velocity by the alarm that it would break the container. Also, you would still have to deal with the levitation in order for this problem to occur.

So, yes, the best and only option is to launch it into space so it can wreck some other planet's day. On a semi-side note, the reason I know it produces waves and not just our mental perception of sound is that it has been shown to destroy materials (such as organs) with it's waves, which would not happen if the effect was merely mnemonic.

item.content:encoded:
I'm going to address both of these.

For those who weren't there:
A simple explanation:

Getting someone TO the moon requires killing multiple people. As far as I know, SCP-120 is the only consistent way to get to the moonbase. It requires a minimum of SIX deaths just to dial it back around to the moon after ONE transfer. D-class are no longer considered cheap and easy resources. Necessary, yes. Casually disposable? Not cost effective. Also, even without an atmosphere, if the volume continues to increase, it WOULD be heard on the moon. The vibrations alone would reach the Lunar base in an hour or two just due to surface contact.

As to SCP-682…SO many reasons.
OK, the first and foremost, the party-line. No cross-experimentation. Why? Well, 682 is an adapter. It CANNOT be killed because it adapts to any threat presented. Therefore this "experiment" will have one of a few possible outcomes. These are the most likely results:

  1. So, maybe it will irritate the worlds (universes?) most dangerous creature, causing a site breach. MORE than 8 deaths, guaranteed.
  2. OR maybe 682 will just adapt to not be bothered by it. Now someone's got to go INTO the enclosure to hit snooze before Site 19 collapses, releasing EVERY Skip on the site. One would surmise that SCP-682 will resist it being turned off. See above.
  3. OR (even better). SCP-682 swallows the device, and adapts to have that ability. On command. At whatever volume it likes. I think that might make for an XK scenario.

People may say "don't bring up 682 on other SCPs." There are reasons. There has never been a successful cross-test outside of the little computer. That wasn't human. I see #2 as the most likely occurance, but there's no good result.

Add to this that SCP-682 is one of the older residents. There was a thread of attempted cross-tests and attempted kills. They were funny, nasty, strange, and became the foundation of what became LolFoundation. Some of us remember the silly OTT days fondly; most don't. Heavy crosstesting, Open testing logs for SCP-173, -500, -914, etc (most of S1) are now a part of site history. EVERY possible suggestion has most likely been made, notwithstanding the volumes of jokes in chat.

TL;DR Been There, DONE THAT (Gave the T-Shirt to SCP-076-2, 'cause he asked nicely)

AS to the SCP we're discussing. I LIKE! Simple. Direct. Intensely dangerous. Strange, but reasonable Containment Protocols. +1!

item.title: Re: Safe?
item.content:encoded:
While it doesn't pass the "Locked Box" test, it does fall under the Safe class description.

The designation "Safe" is assigned to subjects or objects that may be effectively and reliably contained. Safe designates may have individual containment procedures, but these procedures are not expected to fail frequently, or be subject to later revision as more information is obtained about a subject.

It should be noted that Safe does not indicate that the containment procedures are unnecessary. Many Safe-designated objects can be quite dangerous in the right contexts. The important distinction that defines a Safe object is that it can be handled safely with appropriate containment procedures. An example of a Safe object would be a gun, a nuclear weapon, or polonium.

First of all, I kept waiting in vain for the bit at the end of the incident log that explained why the two D-Class were fighting - was it caused by SCP-498 or its effects directly, or was it in issue with the D-Class Personnel themselves? In other words, was the incident caused by the actual SCP object, or was it a matter of making a poor choice with who would be assigned to the job? Just saying that they were fighting kind of falls flat without some sort of explanation; I mean, why would D-4113 have not wanted to follow the procedure if he knew what SCP-498 did?

Second, I thought the deal was that the Foundation is "cold, not cruel"; I'm beginning to think that my definition of "cold" and "cruel" are different from those of everyone else on this website. To me, "cold" means "unwilling to make exceptions or be lenient based on simple human empathy", while "cruel" means "unnecessarily hostile", "going out of one's way to display a lack of empathy", or "the opposite of empathetic". In other words, terminating a D-Class Personnel who earned commendation for preventing a catastrophe falls under the category of "cruel" as opposed to "cold", at least in my books - it's nonsensical, and in some ways counterintuitive, as I'm sure reliable personnel are hard to come by for the Foundation. If this is a matter of a policy that has been in place since after the last time someone edited this article, then my bad, but it should probably still be fixed; if I'm mistaken in how "cold" and "cruel" are defined, please feel free to correct me in my beliefs.

Reminds me of an experience I had with the same model clock radio as in the picture a few days ago. For an hour, I was hearing something that sounded like running water in an adjacent room and I thought maybe they'd left the tap on. It turned out, the clock radio was on and set between two stations. Every single button that I pressed except Snooze had absolutely no effect. When I hit Snooze, the noise stopped for five seconds and then came right back.

I unplugged it. The noise was still there. Then I noticed it had a battery backup. After I removed the battery… it kept making the noise! For two seconds, while it still had some residual charge. Before the noise finally stopped, I was about to put the thing down and get a hammer.

Long story short, I'm upvoting, just because this showed up less than a week after my experience with a haunted clock radio.
